questions.solution_text:
$\theta$ is opposite the $16$ cm side and $28^{\circ}$ is opposite the $10$ cm side.
$\dfrac{\sin\theta}{16}=\dfrac{\sin 28^{\circ}}{10}$
$\sin\theta=\dfrac{16\sin 28^{\circ}}{10}$
$=0.75115\ldots$
The inverse sine gives the acute angle $48.6904\ldots^{\circ}$, and $\theta$ is obtuse.
$\theta=180^{\circ}-48.6904\ldots^{\circ}$
$\approx 131^{\circ}$

The angle opposite the $19$ cm side is $\angle AQC$ in one triangle and $\angle APC$ in the other.
$\dfrac{\sin\theta}{19}=\dfrac{\sin 30^{\circ}}{14}$
$\sin\theta=\dfrac{19\sin 30^{\circ}}{14}$
$=0.67857\ldots$
The inverse sine gives the acute angle $42.7321\ldots^{\circ}$, which is $\angle AQC$.
$\angle AQC\approx 43^{\circ}$
The obtuse partner has the same sine, and it is $\angle APC$.
$\angle APC=180^{\circ}-42.7321\ldots^{\circ}$
$\approx 137^{\circ}$

Find obtuse $\angle PQR$, to the nearest degree.
